JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from respondents on account of death of Jayalakshmamma, who is wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioners No.2 and 3, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 13-09-2021 at about 8:50 a.m., deceased Jayalakshmamma was a pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-11-ED-4640, which was driven by her husband Madegowda, slowly and cautiously in a moderate speed, by observing all traffic norms, on the extreme left side of the road and he was taking right turn by giving indications of taking turn in front of Shivalingaiah shop, Maddur-Tumkur road, near Athaguru village.

At that time the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.
KA-09-EQ-7411 came in very high speed, in rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life and property and dashed to the motorcycle of husband of Jayalakshmamma from behind.
Due to the impact, the Jayalakshmamma fell down on the road and sustained grievous fatal injuries all over her body and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was doing milk vending and agriculturist by profession and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Kesthuru Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.

2 3.
On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.31030031210200156479 valid from 14-09-2021 12.00.01 a.m., to 13-09-2022 11.59.59 p.m., in respect of motorcycle Hero Honda bearing No.KA-09-EQ-7411 in favour of respondent No.1.
However, the alleged accident had occurred on 13-09-2021 at 8.50 a.m.
Hence, as on the date of alleged accident, the above policy was not in force.
Hence, it is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 for any liability that may be fastened on it.
In view of above denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Smt. Jayalakshmamma succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident alleged to have occurred on 13-09-2021 at about 8.50 a.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EQ-7411 ?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.
In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.3 has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 10 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 and closed their side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its Assistant Manager as R.W.1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3 and closed its side.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 13-09-2021 at about 8.50 a.m., deceased Jayalakshmamma was a pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-11- ED-4640, which was driven by her husband Madegowda, slowly and cautiously in a moderate speed, by observing all traffic norms, on the extreme left side of the road and he was taking right turn by giving indications Madegowda vs Varun.P on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163112424/
3 of taking turn in front of Shivalingaiah Shop, Maddur-Tumkur road, near Athaguru Village.

At that time the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EQ-7411 came in very high speed, in rash and negligent manner, so has to endangering human life and property came and dashed to the motorcycle of husband of Jayalakshmamma from behind.
Due to the impact, the Jayalakshmamma fell down on the road and sustained grievous fatal injuries all over her body and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
10. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.3 has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit and got marked total 10 documents as Ex.P.1 to 10.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Sketch, Ex.P.4 is true copy of vehicle seizure mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of Spot Mahazer, Ex.P.6 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.7 is true copy of Inquest Mahazer, Ex.P.8 is true copy of Post-mortem report, Ex.P.9 is true copy of Charge-sheet and Ex.P.10 are notarised copies of Aadhar cards (total 4).

11. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, except the validity of insurance policy issued in favour of respondent No.1 and liability of respondent No.2 to indemnify the respondent No.1, the date, time and place of accident, negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EQ-7411, involvement of vehicles, death of Jayalakshmamma due to injuries caused in the alleged accident, are not in dispute.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 9, prima-facia it reveals that, on 13-09-2021 at about 8.50 a.m., deceased Jayalakshmamma was a pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-11-ED-4640, which was driven by her husband Madegowda, slowly and cautiously in a moderate speed, by observing all traffic norms, on the extreme left side of the road and he was taking right turn in front of Shivalingaiah Shop, Maddur-Tumkur road, near Athaguru Village.
At that time the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EQ-7411 came in very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of husband of Jayalakshmamma from behind.
Due to the impact, the Jayalakshmamma fell down on the road and sustained grievous fatal injuries all over her body and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EQ-7411 the said accident has taken place and the deceased Jayalakshmamma sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to said injuries on the spot.
There is absolutely no evidence placed on record by the respondents to rebut the final report of the investigation officer and other police documents produced by the petitioners.
12. The petitioner No.3, who has been examined as P.W.1, has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
The oral evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence marked as Ex.P.1 to 10.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

13. Further, though, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above facts in his written statement, he has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary Madegowda vs Varun.P on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163112424/
4 evidence placed on record by the petitioners.

It is pertinent to note that, the P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 in his cross-examination that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner No.1, who was the rider of the TVS XL motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-11-ED-4640 and not due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EQ-7411.

On the other hand,
it is not the case of respondent No.2 that, at the time of accident the petitioner No.1 and deceased Jayalakshmamma were not wearing helmet and there is some contributory negligence on their part also.
14.
Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.6 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident had not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not occurred due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of motorcycle rider, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.9, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EQ-7411.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence led by the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner No.1 and there is no negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09- EQ-7411.
Further, the Ex.P.8 Post-motem report, clearly speaks that, deceased Jayalakshmamma, has died due to shock and haemorrhage due to injury to brain as a result of head injury.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Jayalakshmamma, in the said accident.
15.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Jayalakshmamma, has succumbed to the injuries sustained in motor vehicle accident occurred on 13-09-2021 at about 8.50 a.m., in front of Shivalingaiah Shop, Maddur-Tumkur road, near Athaguru Village due to the rash and negligent Madegowda vs Varun.P on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163112424/
5 driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-09-EQ-7411.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that,
the alleged accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending motorcycle, bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EQ-7411 and due to said impact, the deceased Jayalakshmamma sustained grievous injuries on her head and was succumbed to said injuries on the spot.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, they have produced the Aadhar card of deceased Jayalakshmamma, and their respective Aadhar cards, which are marked as Ex.P.10.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is the husband, petitioner No.2 is the daughter and petitioner No.3 is the son of deceased Jayalakshmamma.
The relationship of petitioners with the deceased is not in dispute.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Jayalakshmamma.
19. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "12.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
10. The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.

11. According to Section 2(11) CPC, "legal representative" means a person who in law represents the Tractor and Trally bearing No.AP-03-AN-8690 & AP-03-AN-8712 estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased and where a party sues or is sued in a representative character the person on whom the estate devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued.

Almost in similar terms is the definition of legal representative under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 i.e. under Section 2(1)(g).
12.

As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only.

entities.text: Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Instead it stipulates that, a person who may or may not be legal heir competent to inherit the property of the deceased can represent the estate of the deceased person.
It includes heirs as well as persons who represent the estate even without title either as executors or administrators in possession of the estate of the deceased.
All such persons would be covered by the expression "legal representative".

As observed in Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234 a legal representative is one who Madegowda vs Varun.P on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163112424/
6 suffers on account of death of a person due to a motor vehicle accident and need not necessarily be a wife, husband, parent and child.
13.

sentences.text: In Manjuri Bera (supra), in paragraph 15 of the said decision, while adverting to the provisions of Section 140 of the Act, the Court observed that even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant, if he was a legal representative, will be entitled to compensation.
In the concurring judgment of Justice S. H. Kapadia, as His Lordship then was, it is observed that there is distinction between "right to apply for compensation" and "entitlement to compensation".
The compensation constitutes part of the estate of the deceased.
As a result, the legal representative of the deceased would inherit the estate.
Indeed, in that case, the Court was dealing with the case of a married daughter of the deceased and the efficacy of Section 140 of the Act.
Nevertheless, the principle underlying the exposition in this decision would clearly (claimants) even though they are major sons of the deceased and also earning.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

20. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
21. The compensation towards loss of dependency:
The petitioners No.1 is the husband, petitioner No.2 is the daughter and petitioner No.3 is the son of deceased Jayalakshmamma.
The petitioners have established that, they are legal representatives of the deceased.

Further, they have stated that,
they were depending upon the deceased.
But, the P.W.1 during his cross-examination has clearly admitted that, petitioner No.2 is married.
The petitioner No.2 being a married daughter of deceased is not entitled to claim compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners No.1 and 3 being the husband and son of deceased are only entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased : The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 55 years.
To substantiate this point, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.10 Aadhar Card of deceased Jayalakshmamma, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01-01-1957.
Admittedly, the accident took place on 13-09-2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 65 years.
The petitioners have stated that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was doing milk vending and agriculture work and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.

But, the petitioners have not produced any document Madegowda vs Varun.P on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163112424/
7 to show the deceased Jayalakshmamma was doing milk vending and agriculture work and she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court,
except to consider the notional income as income of the deceased as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another, in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. Mahesh and another in MFA No.140/2017, judgment dated 16-01-2020 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others in MFA No.101195/2014, judgment dated 05-01-2023, has clearly held

that,
"when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2021.

Therefore, the notional income of the deceased as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be treated as Rs.
15,000/- per month.
Therefore, the annual income of the deceased in the present case is held as Rs.1,80,000/-.
ii) As on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 65 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the legal heirs of deceased are not entitled for future prospects of the deceased.

sentences.text: iii) The deduction of personal expenses and calculating the multiplier: The family of the deceased consist of 2 persons i.e., petitioners No.1 and 3.
The total number of the dependents of the deceased are two.
Therefore, deduction towards the personal expenses of deceased is taken as 1/3rd of the total income, which comes to Rs.60,000/-.
After deducting 1/3rd out of total income, towards the personal expenses of deceased, the annual income of the deceased is held as Rs.1,20,000/-.
iv) As on the date of death, the age of the deceased was 65 years.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 7.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency is held as Rs.8,40,000/-.
v) Compensation under conventional heads:
In the present case, admittedly, the petitioner No.1 is the husband, petitioner No.2 is the daughter and petitioner No.3 is the son of deceased Jayalakshmamma.
Hence, the petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation under the head of filial consortium.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the compensation under the following conventional heads is awarded:
 a) Loss of estate - Rs. 15,000/-

b ) Loss of consortium - Rs. 40,000/-
 c) Funeral expenses - Rs. 15,000/-

8 The compensation under above heads has to be enhanced 10% for every 3 years.
Seven years have been lapsed from the date of the judgment.

Therefore, the compensation under the above conventional heads is enhanced by 20%, the loss of estate comes to Rs.18,000/-, the loss of filial consortium comes to Rs.48,000/- each to petitioner No.1 to 3 and funeral expenses comes to Rs.18,000/-.
22.

Accordingly, the petitioners No.1 and 3 are entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
 Sl. Head of  Amount/Rs  No. Compensation  1. Loss of dependency Rs. 8,40,000-00  2. Loss of filial consortium Rs. 96,000-00  3. Loss of estate Rs. 18,000-00  4. Funeral expenses Rs. 18,000-00

Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners No.1 and 3 together are entitled for compensation of Rs. 9,72,000/- and the petitioner No.2 is entitled for compensation of Rs.48,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
23. Now the question before this Court is, who is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA- 09-EQ-7411.

The petitioners have specifically contended that, as on the date of accident the respondent No.2 was the insurer of offending vehicle and hence,
the respondent No.2 liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 for the liability that may be fastened on the respondent No.1.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 has denied the alleged fact and specifically contended that, as on the date of accident the insurance policy issued in favour of the respondent No.1 was not in force.

The policy No.31030031210200156479, issued by the respondent No.2 in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EQ-7411, was valid from 14-09-2021 12:00:01 A.M., to 13-09-2022 11:59:59 P.M.
The alleged accident has occurred on 13-09-2021 at 08:50 A.M., i.e. before the commencement of risk period of insurance policy.

Hence,
the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Madegowda vs Varun.P on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163112424/
9 24.

Admittedly, as per Ex.R.2 Insurance Policy bearing No.31030031210200156479, issued by the respondent No.2 in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of offending motorcycle bearing No.
KA-09-EQ-7411, was valid from 14- 09-2021 12:00:01 A.M., to 13-09-2022 11:59:59 P.M.
Further, it is clearly mentioned in the said insurance policy that, the respondent No.1 has paid premium amount of Rs.1,349/- under receipt No.31030081210000156035, on 11-09-2021 itself.

25. The learned counsel for petitioners vehemently argued that, as the respondent No.2 has received premium amount on 11-09-2021 and issued receipt in favour of respondent No.1, the risk coverage under said policy starts from the 11-09-2021 itself and not from the date of issuance of policy certificate.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued that, it is clearly mentioned in Ex.R.2 Insurance Policy Certificate that, the period of risk coverage is from 14-09- 2021 12:00:01 A.M., to 13-09-2022 11:59:59 P.M., and as the accident has taken place on 13-09-2021 at 08:50 A.M., i.e. before the commencement of risk period, the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has relied on the following decisions:
i) Reliance Life Insurance Company Ltd. & another V/s Jaya Wadhwani, reported in (2024) 1 S.C.R. 65, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has clearly held that, " In the present appeals, we do not find any such issue of back dating, but the date of issuance of the policy would be the relevant date for all the purposes and not the date of proposal or the date of issuance of the receipt.

entities.text: Reliance Life Insurance Company Ltd. & another V/s Jaya Wadhwani, reported in (2024) 1 S.C.R. 65
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, the stand taken by the appellant is approved.

The impugned orders are this liable to be set aside."
ii) Samilulla and another V/s Mehatabulla @ Mehatab and another, reported in ILR 2022 Kar 3880,
the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has clearly held that, " a) Normally, the insurance is a contract between the insurer and insured that determines rights and liabilities between the parties.

entities.text: Samilulla and another V/s Mehatabulla @ Mehatab and another, reported in ILR 2022 Kar 3880
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The owner of vehicle submits his proposal of insurance to the Insurer-Company and pays premium required to consider his proposal to cover the risks.
On accepting of said proposal by Insurer, both enter into a contract, agreeing to certain terms and conditions and issues policy of insurance.
The insurer thereafter promises to pay for loss caused by perils, covered under the policy of insurance.
Since it is contract between insurer and insured, the provisions of the Indian Contract Act is applicable to them along with Motor Vehicles Act.
b) Respondent No.1 has produced proposal form of insuring of his vehicle at Ex.R.4.
It was submitted on 21-05-2015.
Time of submission of said proposal is not indicated on the said document.
However, in the column, "for office use only", it is mentioned that the vehicle was inspected on 21-05-2015 at 4.10 p.m.
It is also pertinent to note that in Ex.R.4 it self, it is mentioned that the period of insurance was from 22-05-2015 to 21-05-2016.

The contents of the said proposal form itself clearly reveals that liability of insurer commences from 22-05-2015 at 00.00 hours and ends on 21-05-2016.

sentences.text:
In such circumstances, when by clear terms both the parties,
i.e respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 had agreed that the liability of respondent No.2 shall commences from 14-09- 2021 12:00:01 A.M. and ends on 13-09-2022 11:59:59 P.M., now the respondent No.1 cannot claim that, he paid the premium on 11-09-2021 itself and therefore the liability of respondent No.2 insurance company commences immediately after the receipt of premium amount and same is not sustainable in the eye of law.
Further, as the accident has taken place on 13-09-2021 at 08:50 A.M., i.e. before the commencement of risk period, the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Further, when the Ex.R.2 insurance policy was itself not in force as on the date of accident, the question of directing the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and recover the same from the respondent No.1 does not arise at all.

27. Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EQ-7411 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.

As the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending vehicle was not in force on the alleged date and time of accident, the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners No.1 & 3 together are entitled for compensation of Rs. 9,72,000/- and the petitioner No.2 is entitled for compensation of Rs.48,000/- from the respondent No.1, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners No.1 and 3 together are entitled for compensation of Rs.9,72,000/-

p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The petitioners No.2 is entitled for compensation of Rs. 48,000/- (Rupees forty-eight thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 liable to pay the above compensation amount and he is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.

The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Husband - 60% Petitioner No.3 - Son - 40% Out of total compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioners No.1 and 3, 40% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their names Madegowda vs Varun.P on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163112424/
12 as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 60% amount with proportionate interest shall be released through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded in favour of petitioner No.2 shall be released in her favour through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
The petition against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from respondents on account of death of Jayalakshmamma, who is wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioners No.2 and 3, in a road traffic accident.
Due to the impact, the Jayalakshmamma fell down on the road and sustained grievous fatal injuries all over her body and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was doing milk vending and agriculturist by profession and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
